lede: Singapore is dealing with haze and showers while the government puts S$45 million behind factory AI, Jio's record IPO opens for bidding in India, and Anthropic's compute and policy moves keep making news ahead of its November listing.
today: Bidding opens for Jio Platforms' US$3.2 billion IPO, and the N95 mask stockpile reaches supermarket shelves as the haze continues.

threads.title: The haze
threads.status: Smoke from Sumatra fires has kept the PSI in the unhealthy range on and off for a week. The health ministry has released its N95 stockpile to retailers, and the government is pressing Indonesia over which companies' land is burning.

threads.title: Anthropic's listing
threads.status: Anthropic is expected to list in November. This week brought its draft safety bill, reports of strained cloud partnerships, and a new Singapore office with nine local roles.

stocks_note: Latest completed closes: New York, Tuesday 20 October (AAPL, GOOGL) and SGX, Tuesday 20 October (DBS), via Yahoo Finance. No earnings dates turned up in today's sources.
applied: more Singapore business, as you asked on Monday

sections.title: The week in five
sections.subtitle: Fridays: the five stories that mattered this week

items.headline: Haze returned and the government went after the companies behind it
items.summary: After a short respite the smoke came back over Singapore, PSI readings spent several days in the unhealthy range, and the health ministry pushed its N95 stockpile to retailers. Ministers said publicly that they are pressing Indonesia over which firms' concessions are burning, a harder line than in past haze seasons.

items.headline: Jio Platforms opened India's largest ever IPO
items.summary: Reliance's digital arm opened bidding for a US$3.2 billion listing, the biggest in Indian history, with retail investors allotted a large tranche. Demand on the first day was strong despite a soft week for the Sensex, and the pricing sets a marker for every other Indian tech company thinking about going public.

items.headline: Anthropic spent the week preparing the ground for its listing
items.summary: A draft federal safety bill, a Singapore office with nine roles, and reports of friction with its cloud partners all landed in five days. Taken together they read as a company shaping the regulatory and operational story investors will hear in November, with compute supply the open question.

items.headline: Russia freed Stephen Hubbard as talks with Washington resumed
items.summary: The 74-year-old teacher walked free in St Petersburg while envoy Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin, with no prisoner swap. Trump said he asked for it personally. It is the second American released in two months and came as both sides said technical talks on Ukraine would continue.

items.headline: Open models got cheaper to run, from both sides of the Pacific
items.summary: DeepSeek open-sourced its inference engine, Google and Amazon shipped tools to move PyTorch code off Nvidia GPUs, and OpenAI put its models on Google Cloud. Different motives, same effect: the cost of serving a model is falling faster than the cost of training one, and Nvidia's software moat is being tested.

sections.title: The week ahead
sections.subtitle: Sundays: what to watch in the coming days

items.headline: Jio Platforms' IPO closes and allotments follow
items.summary: Bidding for the US$3.2 billion listing runs through the week, with allotment and the listing date to follow. Watch the subscription multiple on the final day; it will set the tone for the other Indian tech IPOs queued behind it, and for how retail investors feel about the Sensex after a soft week.

items.headline: Haze readings, and whether the N95 stockpile holds
items.summary: The NEA's daily PSI forecast is the number to check each morning. The health ministry said masks would reach all major supermarkets progressively; if shelves empty again this week, expect pressure for a second release and more detail on which Indonesian concessions are burning.

items.headline: Anthropic's listing timetable and any pricing range
items.summary: With a November debut expected, a public filing or price range could land any day. The things to read in it: the size of the compute commitments to Google and Amazon, how much revenue runs through those two partners, and whether the Singapore office appears in the regional plans.

sections.title: Apple
sections.subtitle: Official news in brief, then 9to5Mac and MacRumors

official.label: From Apple
official.summary: Apple named new American supplier partners for iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, covering critical materials and components, and expanded earlier commitments. It also opened its Designers of Tomorrow showcase with Design Miami in Paris, themed around presence. iPhone Duo pre-orders began on 16 October, and a new Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini landed earlier this month.

items.headline: Apple revokes eight web certificates scammers could abuse, but Macs may still trust them
items.summary: Apple has blocked eight web security certificates that could have let fraudsters pose as genuine websites. A cryptography engineer warns that Macs may keep trusting the compromised certificates, so the underlying weakness has not been closed yet.

items.headline: iPhone Duo review: a compact foldable that changes the iPhone shape
items.summary: The first reviews call the iPhone Duo the biggest change to the iPhone form factor in almost 20 years. It pairs a compact, notebook-style body with an iPad-like inner display. It looks a little awkward, but the reviewer says there are good reasons for that.

items.headline: Loop Capital drops Apple to Hold on weaker iPhone outlook
items.summary: The analyst firm cut Apple from Buy to Hold, arguing the company is unlikely to recover an estimated 13 million iPhone units trimmed from its second-half 2026 plans. The call is relayed through an Investing.com report.
items.why: You hold AAPL: one analyst downgrade on iPhone outlook, two weeks before results.

items.headline: UK regulator proposes easing the way for Apple Pay rivals
items.summary: The Competition and Markets Authority wants changes that would make it easier and cheaper for other companies to offer payment options on the iPhone. The proposals take aim at Apple's fees and the way access to the phone's tap-to-pay hardware is handled.

items.headline: Why Singapore finds it hard to pin haze fires on specific companies
items.summary: Enforcement of the haze law is held back by cross-border investigations and the difficulty of gathering evidence. Experts discuss how the law could be strengthened as smoke from the region returns to Singapore skies this week.

items.headline: MOH releases its N95 mask stockpile to help retailers meet haze demand
items.summary: The Ministry of Health has opened up its stock of N95 or equivalent masks so retailers can keep up with public demand during the haze. Pet owners are also seeing effects, with some vets reporting up to 15 per cent more eye and breathing cases.
items.why: Worth a box of N95s at home before the shelves clear again.

items.headline: COE premiums climb again in first tender after the system review was announced
items.summary: Category A closed at S$132,004 and Category B at S$131,901 in the first tender since the COE review was announced, leaving Category A just short of September's S$133,009 record. The Land Transport Authority says demand stays high ahead of a coming car exhibition, so buyers should not expect quick relief.

items.headline: Singapore adds S$135 million for coastal protection and flood research
items.summary: The new money builds on the S$125 million used in 2023 to set up the Coastal Protection and Flood Management Research Programme. It extends work on defending a low-lying island against rising seas and heavier rain.

items.headline: Jio Platforms opens bidding for a US$3.2 billion IPO
items.summary: The listing is expected to be an offer for sale, so existing investors sell shares and Jio raises no new capital. It is billed as India's biggest public offering and is being watched as a test of appetite for large tech issues.

items.headline: SBI confirms 3,897 customer records surfaced on the dark web
items.summary: State Bank of India told the exchanges that a preliminary review of about 375,000 records posted on the dark web found 3,897 genuine customer entries, with phone numbers, dates of birth, email and home addresses. It was alerted on 16 October by CERT-In and its threat-intelligence provider, and says it does not yet know where the data came from.

items.headline: Delhi Police seek a three-day custody extension for two CJP leaders
items.summary: Delhi Police asked a court on Wednesday for three more days of judicial custody for Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, among 14 people detained on 13 October after allegedly entering Jantar Mantar a day after it was denotified as a protest site. The two had earlier withdrawn a High Court challenge to a two-day extension.

items.headline: Tamil Nadu on alert as a new Bay of Bengal system keeps heavy rain going until 26 October
items.summary: The regional weather centre expects intense rainfall to persist, with warnings issued to residents along the Palar river and a school holiday declared in Chennai. The state is also repairing rainwater harvesting structures ahead of the northeast monsoon.

items.headline: Russia frees US citizen Stephen Hubbard as a Trump envoy meets Putin
items.summary: Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired teacher from Michigan held since 2022 on charges of fighting as a mercenary in Ukraine, was freed in St Petersburg while envoy Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin. Trump says he asked for the release and gave nothing in return; the Kremlin cited Hubbard's poor health.

items.headline: France argues over who is to blame for some of its worst urban unrest in decades
items.summary: Cost-of-living protests turned into riots in several cities, with Apple stores looted and the historic city hall in Limoges gutted by fire. Overnight curfews now cover central Paris and Lyon. Macron blames far-left activists and says Trump spread false claims about migrants, while analysts disagree on what set the violence off.

items.headline: Musk confirms Tesla and SpaceX are weighing a merger
items.summary: On SpaceX's earnings call, Musk said both boards have set up special committees of independent directors, at shareholders' request, to study combining the two companies. He is excluded from the talks as a conflicted party, no terms have been agreed, and a Tesla deal would need a majority of all outstanding shares.

items.headline: Iran's enriched uranium resurfaces as a sticking point in talks with the US
items.summary: Tehran insists enrichment is its right under the Non-Proliferation Treaty, while Washington wants a meaningful cut in capacity and part of the stockpile moved abroad. Iran calls the material a national asset but has not ruled out diluting it at home under monitors. The IAEA's last estimate was about 440 kg enriched to 60 percent.

sections.title: Explainer
sections.subtitle: One idea from today's news, in plain words

brief.label: What an inference engine does, and why DeepSeek gave one away
brief.summary:
Training a model is the expensive part everyone talks about. Serving it, which is called inference, is the part that costs money every single day. An inference engine is the software that takes a trained model and answers requests as cheaply and quickly as possible: it batches many users' prompts together, keeps the right numbers in the right memory, and skips work it can predict.
DeepSeek's DeepInfer is that software for its own models, released free under an open licence. Two things make that interesting. It runs on Huawei's Ascend chips as well as Nvidia's, which makes Chinese hardware a little more usable for everyone. And it pushes down the price of serving open models, which is the fight DeepSeek wants: if open models are cheap to run, closed rivals have to compete on something other than cost.
For a product person the takeaway is simple: model quality gets the headlines, but serving cost decides what you can afford to ship.

Enterprise Singapore will put more than S$45 million over three years into helping smaller manufacturers adopt ready-made AI tools, announced at ITAP 2026. At Cyber Week, K Shanmugam asked AI companies for full and immediate transparency when incidents occur, and OpenAI backed the idea. Separately, NTU was ranked first globally in AI in a new university ranking.

sections.title: AI startups in Singapore and Southeast Asia
sections.subtitle: Up to three stories from the past week

items.headline: Genie Health, from ex-PropertyGuru CEO Hari Krishnan, raises US$3 million seed
items.summary: The healthtech startup uses AI to help people make sense of their own medical data, from wearables to records, through a free app that stores health records and a SmartCare tool that helps clinics book follow-up visits. The round announced today includes Liminal, the Temasek-backed venture studio, and funds product build-out and early hiring.

items.headline: Moonshot AI, maker of Kimi, appears to be setting up in Singapore
items.summary: A new sales role listed on the company's LinkedIn page as of 20 October points to a Singapore operation, Business Times reports. It is an early sign the Chinese AI lab wants a regional commercial presence.

sections.title: AI worldwide
sections.subtitle: Models and products, money, policy and chips

items.headline: DeepSeek open-sources an internal framework for running models cheaply
items.summary: DeepSeek has released DeepInfer, the inference engine behind its own services, under an Apache 2.0 licence. It runs DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Nvidia's newest GPUs and Huawei's Ascend 950 chips and was built largely on vLLM. A senior researcher framed it as part of a push for open models to win outright; the speed claims are DeepSeek's own.

items.headline: Google joins Amazon in helping PyTorch developers leave Nvidia GPUs
items.summary: Google has open-sourced TorchTPU, which lets existing PyTorch code run on its TPUs with a configuration change rather than a rewrite, days after Amazon did the same for Trainium with TorchNeuron. An agent suite helps port apps and fix errors. Both target Nvidia's CUDA software moat, though performance on the new chips is unproven.

items.headline: OpenAI will sell its top models on Google Cloud
items.summary: Google Cloud is adding GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, plus Codex workflows, to its Model Garden as a private preview for selected enterprise customers, with wider access in the coming weeks. Usage lands on the customer's Google invoice. It follows OpenAI's split from Microsoft exclusivity and its AWS debut in April.

items.headline: OpenAI buys Orchestra Bio to build out its life-sciences work
items.summary: OpenAI has bought Orchestra Bio, a four-year-old startup whose agents take on study monitoring and timeline tracking for drug-development teams, for an undisclosed sum. The team and technology join Rosalind, OpenAI's life-sciences suite, alongside the GPT-Rosalind model and the Rosalind Workbench tool for planning experiments and analysing results.

items.headline: Anthropic's cloud partnerships are reportedly getting messy before its November IPO
items.summary: Google, Amazon and Microsoft increasingly see Anthropic as a competitor, and the company says they have not supplied all the compute it asked for even as its infrastructure bill balloons. Nearly half its sales last year ran through Amazon and Google, a dependence that investors will be weighing ahead of next month's listing.
items.counter: Anthropic's own filing frames the same facts as planned capacity growth rather than a shortfall.

items.headline: Anthropic pitches an AI safety bill with a judge-approval step
items.summary: Anthropic's draft federal bill, first reported by Politico, would let the government block a frontier model only for a foreseeable, imminent risk of more than US$1 billion in damage or 50 or more deaths, and only after the Commerce Department persuades a judge in Washington. No agency could act alone. Critics say the bar is far too high.
items.why: AI governance is on your course list; this bill is the clearest current example of industry drafting its own rules.

items.headline: China sets up a state-owned firm in Xiongan to manage national data for AI
items.summary: China National Data Group, launched in Xiongan on Monday as the 100th centrally run state enterprise, is backed by the big telecoms and power utilities and overseen by SASAC. Its job is to pool national data resources, break down regional and industry silos, and secure a supply of training data for domestic AI models.

items.headline: Alibaba says chips using its RISC-V design have shipped more than 6 billion units
items.summary: Damo Academy's chief scientist told the RISC-V Summit in Shenzhen that chips built on its XuanTie designs have passed six billion cumulative units, a company-reported figure. It also unveiled the E908A automotive core with ASIL-D safety support and promised a C950A chip for autonomous driving by the end of 2027.
